Hi Ben —

Great to hear you're progressing. Quick summary of a suggested approach so we can align on cost vs SLA tradeoffs before the call:

High-level recommendation (starter allocation)
- Reserve: A100-80 (40% of baseline slots) + L4 (30%) — A100-80 for long-context summarization and mixed workloads, L4 for conversational baseline throughput where latency matters but model size is smaller.
- Burst-only: H100 for peak long-context runs or large-batch exports where higher FP8 throughput helps reduce tail latency/cost (commercial burst pool).

Why this split
- Memory vs performance: A100-80 gives enough memory headroom for 8k sequences without excessive tiling; it is a cost-effective reserve. L4 gives excellent per-token cost and lower latency for short contexts at high QPS. H100 is great for heavy multi-stream long-context or when fp8 kernels materially reduce per-token time — ideal as burst.

Operational levers we recommend enabling:
- Per-route model mapping: pin chat to L4-optimized variant, pin summarization to A100-80 variant with larger kv-cache limits.
- Prefix/KV caching for repeated system prompts to reduce afternoon cost by ~10–20%.
- Tail-aware routing: keep a small headroom of reserved A100 slots (10–15%) for long-context steady traffic and allow H100 burst for scheduled batch windows.

I've looped in Dev to provide a technical sizing workbook and a quick numeric sketch. Can you confirm: target committed vGPU slots (monthly) you are comfortable with and peak QPS for chat?

I attached an initial worksheet for your review. We'll update with numbers after Dev's note. Call proposed: Wed 12/9 10:30am PT — does that work?

Thanks,

Hi all —

I ran quick back-of-envelope capacity scenarios from the sample profiles. Key numbers / assumptions are below (feel free to push back):

Assumptions
- short chat model: 6B dense / quantized to 8-bit -> fits comfortably on L4 (24GB) with per-stream KV cache for 128 tokens. Average latency target: <= 80ms p95.
- long context model: 70B / requires ~60–70GB KV + activations at 8k tokens -> A100-80 recommended for reserve to avoid excessive tiling.
- embeddings: batched 8k vectors, throughput-optimized path; L4 can service many small batches but large embedding jobs benefit from H100 fp8 for lower per-token cost when parallelized.

Starter numeric sketch (monthly committed slots -> estimated effective concurrent streams):
- Reserve 8 x A100-80 (steady long-context headroom) -> supports ~12 concurrent long-context sessions at 8k (depends on exact model memory).
- Reserve 12 x L4 -> supports ~240 short chat concurrent sessions (128-token avg) with autoscaling buffer.
- Keep H100 as a burst pool (no reserved commit initially) sized to peak batch windows: 4 x H100 for 2-4 hour nightly batches.

Cost & risk notes
- A100 reservation reduces latency risk for long-context; switching to H100-reserve reduces latency further but roughly doubles reserve cost for the same memory headroom.
- L4 reserve is high QPS and cost-efficient but will not fit very large (>70B) models. If Quantify plans to move to 100k token contexts in 2027, recommend a reserve re-eval.

Operational recommendations
- Model version pinning: deploy identical model variants tuned for each SKU to avoid unpredictable perf regressions.
- Autoscaler rules: aggressive horizontal scale on L4 route; conservative on A100 to preserve memory headroom.
- Fallback: on A100 slot exhaustion, route non-latency-critical summarization jobs to H100-burst when available; enqueue or degrade quality gracefully otherwise.

I'll update the attached workbook with estimated monthly token math and TCO scenarios prior to the 12/9 call.
